title: Five adapter slots — connect lifecycle
scope: Actual lifecycle module exercised with local fake adapters whose connect() resolves, rejects, or never settles. No real sidecar, adapter persistence or startup fault injection against a running server.

defects_closed.L1_aggregate_timeout: One deadline PER SLOT replaces the single 10 s race. Exceeding it is a connect FAILURE for that slot, identical in consequence to a rejection. The failed instance is QUARANTINED before any replacement is attempted, so a connect that settles late finds an object nobody can dispatch into. Late settles (resolved or rejected) are recorded on the readiness record and cannot re-arm the slot; the abandoned promise is handled at source so a late rejection is never an unhandled rejection.
defects_closed.L2_silent_replacement_failure: If the off replacement cannot be constructed, the slot is left quarantined and marked unavailable, logged at error level. The degraded original is never left wired: dispatch throws AdapterQuarantined.
defects_closed.L3_no_per_slot_readiness: Every slot ends in exactly one state (off | ready | disabled | unavailable) with the reason, failure mode (rejected | timeout | replacement-failed), the deadline applied, the duration and any late settle. Published on the app as adapterReadiness; toLegacyHealth() keeps the existing healthy/degraded/off /health vocabulary.

policy.connect_timeout: [adapters] connect_timeout_ms (number) or a per-slot table with a `default` key; a non-positive or non-finite value falls back to 10000 rather than failing every slot.
policy.fail_closed_slots: orchestrator aborts startup on rejection AND on timeout — an orchestrator that never connects is operationally identical to one that refused — and is never silently replaced with off.
policy.quarantine: Own properties and the whole prototype chain are neutered; underscore-private helpers and disconnect() are exempt so shutdown can still release resources. The refusal is async, so it arrives as a rejected promise like every other adapter error.
